claims.text: Mild-to-moderate deficits: increased PO Na and water when pts are conscious and not vomiting.
claims.quote: Mild-to-moderate volume deficits may be replaced by increased oral intake of sodium and water when patients are conscious and not vomiting

claims.text: Severe deficits, or PO replacement impractical: IV 0.9% saline or a buffered electrolyte solution (eg, Ringer's lactate).
claims.quote: When volume deficits are severe or when oral fluid replacement is impractical, IV 0.9% saline or a buffered electrolyte solution (eg, Ringer's lactate) is given.

claims.text: Buffered solutions have lower chloride and may reduce hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis.
claims.quote: Both are well tolerated and safe, but Ringer’s lactate and other buffered solutions have lower chloride concentrations and may reduce development of hyperchloremic metabolic acidosis.

claims.text: Some evidence favors Ringer's lactate over saline, but the issue isn't settled.
claims.quote: Some evidence seems to favor use of Ringer's lactate over saline, but the issue is not settled (1, 2, 3).
